title: add transactional downgrade guard + backup/restore and schema migration safety for private-installer
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Motivation: private-installer upgrades that involve DB schema migrations and component version changes need a transactional, observable guard to prevent unsafe downgrades and to guarantee backup/restore consistency. This PR implements a transactional downgrade-guard that ties together: (1) version pinning metadata stored in the installer state, (2) coordinated Postgres schema migrations with transactional verification, and (3) backup/restore pre- and post-checks to ensure rollbacks are safe. The goal is to make upgrades and rollbacks for on-prem/VPC customers deterministic and reversible when possible, and to fail fast with clear runbooks when not. Change summary: add a new transactional guard component to the installer that records a pre-upgrade snapshot and version manifest, runs schema migrations inside a controlled transactional flow (where feasible), and performs post-migration integrity checks; extend the backup/restore job templates and upgrade controller to include pre-upgrade backup triggers and post-restore validation; add a downgrade prevention check that enforces version pinning and offers an explicit force path with documented manual steps. Checklist: - [x] design doc and runbook (internal link: https://linear.app/ENG/4121/upgrade-downgrade-transactional-guard) - [x] unit + integration tests for migration coordinator - [x] helm chart changes for backup-job + migration-job templates - [x] terraform variables for version pinning and force-rollback flags - [x] e2e upgrade/rollback canary in perf-canary environment - [x] release notes and customer-facing runbook entry Testing & validation: ran canary upgrade on perf-canary cluster (see CI e2e logs), validated that backups are created and restored correctly, and simulated failed migrations to confirm the rollback path. Rollout plan: merge to main, ship as opt-in flag in next installer release, enable by default after one release cycle of canaries and customer validation. Rollback and emergency procedure: installer will refuse automatic downgrade if version-manifest mismatch detected; operator can follow documented manual steps to force-rollback after taking export and support involvement. Notes: this change touches critical installer code paths; special attention applied to observability (detailed events/metrics) and idempotency of the migration coordinator. See related issues: SUP-842, ENG-4121.
